# Superframe nodes

171 technique nodes in 17 lanes, and 31 converters. Port types are in the first table; every node follows.

## Port types

| Type | Shape |
|---|---|
| `field` | Scalar or vector grid. { w, h, channels: 1 | 2, data: Float32Array(w*h*channels) }. Scalar fields are 0..1 by convention; vector fields are signed px per unit. |
| `raster` | Float RGBA picture. { w, h, data: Float32Array(w*h*4) }, linear light, straight (not premultiplied) alpha, 0..1 (light may exceed 1 before export). |
| `vector` | Paths. { w, h, paths: [{ pts: [[x, y], ...], closed?, width?, widths?: number[], fill?: hex, stroke?: hex }] } in px of the w x h frame. |
| `glyphs` | Lettering. { text, w, h, mask: Float32Array(w*h) coverage 0..1, outlines?: vector paths }. text is the real-text equivalent and is always kept. |
| `particles` | Point set. { w, h, n, x: Float32Array(n), y: Float32Array(n), size?: Float32Array(n) px radius, tone?: Float32Array(n) 0..1 }. |
| `audio` | Sample buffer. { rate, channels: [Float32Array, ...] } planar, -1..1. rate is one of the superstack sample rates (48000 by default). |
| `events` | Timed events (MIDI-like). { duration (s), events: [{ t (s), voice, args: { note (MIDI), dur (s), vel 0..1, ... }, role? }] }. Same shape as the studio score. |
| `series` | Data series. { y: Float64Array, x?: Float64Array, label?, unit? }. Raw values, not normalised. |
| `material` | A studio material (schema studio.material/1, studio/lib/schema.mjs): core physical and perceptual numbers plus lane hints. |
| `text` | Language. { text, lang?: BCP 47 tag, role?: content | description }. Words as a medium: they can be set as glyphs, spoken through a spectrogram, or read as they are. |
| `motion` | Moving picture. { w, h, fps, frames: [Float32Array(w*h*4)] linear RGBA, captions?: [{ from, to (frame indices), text }] }. Captions carry the words a story tells, so motion always has a text equivalent. |
| `score` | A criterion. { name, value, target?: [lo, hi], pass?: bool, metrics: { name: number } }. Quality-spec and gate readings travel as scores, so a graph can be steered by a goal. |
| `distribution` | A probability distribution as a value. { kind: normal | uniform | lognormal | choice, mean?, sd?, min?, max?, options?, weights? }. A node can sample it (seeded) or hold it (its mean or mode). |
| `time` | A clock. { t (s), duration (s), fps }. Nodes that animate read it; a still renders at t. |

## Lane: criteria

### `measure.picture`: Measure a picture into a score

Contrast, edge density, clipping and level coverage, folded into one value in 0..1 with each metric kept. The explorer uses the full Python quality tools; this is the in-graph reading a goal can steer by.

Source: `superframe (in-graph proxies for QUALITY-SPEC R2, R4, R6)`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: perception.

Inputs: `raster` raster. Outputs: `score` score.

| Parameter | Range | Default | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | 0 to 1 | 0.6 | score to pass |

### `study.colour`: Colour study of a picture

Palette by k-means in CIELAB with area shares; Goethe contrast-of-extension balance distance on the measured L* scale (the score value, 0 = in balance) and on Goethe's light numbers; hue concentration, colourfulness, value key and composition coherence as metrics. The rebuilt raster paints each pixel with its swatch.

Source: `superframe lib/study (colour criterion)`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: colour science, perception, painting.

Inputs: `raster` raster. Outputs: `score` score, `raster` raster.

| Parameter | Range | Default | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k` | 1 to 24 | 8 | swatches at most |
| `target` | 0 to 1 | 0.3 | largest balance distance that passes |

### `marble.concepts`: Marbling between ideas

Each source is a study: its concepts with weights, laid in one drop as wedges (or rings), each covering its weight share, then marbled with the other studies. The picture is coloured by concept; the text is the reading: each concept's share of the bath, the borders inside one study, and the meetings across studies, which the marbling made and no single study held.

Source: `lib/marble/bath.mjs readElements, conceptReading`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: marbling, concept mapping, provenance.

Inputs: none. Outputs: `raster` raster, `labels` field, `reading` text.

### `spectral.metamers`: Metamers of one colour

Samples the set of reflectances an observer cannot tell apart from the chosen colour under D65 (hit-and-run in the null space of the observer's rows, bands kept in (0.001, 0.999)). Top band: each member under D65 as the standard observer sees it. Bottom band: the same members under the second light, where they part. The vector draws their spectra; the text gives the match error and the spread. A dichromat observer has two rows, so its set is larger and visibly varied to the standard observer even under D65.

Source: `lib/medium/metamers.mjs metamerSet, spread`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: colour science, perception, optics.

Inputs: none. Outputs: `raster` raster, `vector` vector, `reading` text.

| `light` | A, candle | A |  |
| `observer` | standard, protan, deutan, tritan | standard |  |
| `count` | 2 to 128 | 24 | metamers |

### `spectral.hidden`: Hidden by candlelight

Each colour of the day picture gets two extreme metamers (linear programming: smallest and largest candle-lit luminance while matching exactly under D65). Each pixel blends them by the brightness of the hidden picture. Under D65 the result matches the day picture (worst delta E about 4e-6 in tests); by candlelight the hidden picture appears (luminance change correlates 0.99 with it in tests). The hidden picture can only move each colour within the range its metamer set allows: saturated, very dark and very light colours carry little.

Source: `lib/medium/hidden.mjs makeHidden, lpMax`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: colour science, optics, perception.

### `bio.nuclei`: Nuclei by the measured packing law

Nuclei placed by random sequential addition with a hard core, phi / sqrt(density). phi 0.365 reproduces the tissue median Clark-Evans R 1.263 (random placement: 1.05); unfitted, it also lands the Voronoi side-count spread near tissue (1.33 against 1.28; random 1.62). phi 0 is random placement. Outputs the nuclei, the cells as a raster (membrane lines dark, nuclei stained) and the distance to the nearest nucleus.

### `bio.vessels`: Vessels by the measured branching laws

Each segment splits in two. The children's diameters obey d0^x = d1^x + d2^x with x 1.47 (measured; Murray's cube law, x 3, is the control and overshoots the measured child size, 0.88 against 0.71 of the parent), their asymmetry and the angle between them are sampled from the measured spread (angle median 80.5 degrees), and the thinner child turns further, by Murray's split. Segments run about 14.5 diameters. Outputs the tree as tapered paths and painted.

Source: `lib/bio/vessels.mjs grow; laws from ARCADE coronary angiography, CC0; measures/vessellaws-arcade.json`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: physiology, fluids, geometry.

Inputs: none. Outputs: `vector` vector, `raster` raster.

| Parameter | Range | Default | Unit |

| `exponent` | 1 to 4 | 1.47 | branching exponent x (3 is Murray) |
| `bend` | 0 to 0.6 | 0.12 | radians of wander per step |
| `ink` | text | #5a1620 |  |
| `ground` | text | #efe6da |  |

### `bio.bacteria`: Bacteria by the measured shape law

Cells as stadiums, length and width sampled from the measured spread per species. The law: rods lengthen at a near-constant width (slope of log width on log length 0.038 for E. coli, 0.018 for B. subtilis; 0.62 for S. aureus cocci through the same measurement). law isotropic is the control: cells as scaled copies of one shape (slope 1). Placed without overlap.

Source: `lib/bio/bacteria.mjs place, outline; law from DeepBacs StarDist MIXED, CC BY 4.0; measures/bactlaws-deepbacs.json`. Runtime: node, browser. Fields: microbiology, geometry.
